stemMd:
Which choice most logically completes the text?

Okonkwo's results suggest that if vehicle traffic were to destroy the soil crusts across a large area of the basin, then rainfall on that ground would ______

options.label: A
options.textMd: run off more slowly than it did while the crusts were intact.

options.label: B
options.textMd: become less frequent than it had been while the crusts were intact.

options.label: C
options.textMd: soak in less deeply than it did while the crusts were intact.

options.label: D
options.textMd: kill the shrubs growing between the crusted patches within a single season.

explanationMd:
An inference item asks for the conclusion the text most directly supports — nothing larger.

The experiment compared intact crusts with scraped ones. Scraping is a physical removal of the crust, which is exactly what heavy vehicle traffic would do. In the scraped plots water reached 6.1 cm rather than 9.4 cm, so removing crusts over a wide area should reduce penetration depth in the same way. That is choice A.

Check an inference by asking: could I point to the sentence that makes this almost certain? For A the answer is the results sentence. For every other choice there is no such sentence — which is the fastest way to eliminate them.

distractorRationale.b: This confuses how much rain falls with what happens to rain after it lands. The study measured penetration depth only; nothing in the text connects soil crusts to rainfall frequency.
distractorRationale.a: This reverses the mechanism. Okonkwo says the crust's ridged surface is what slows runoff, so removing the crust should make runoff faster, not slower.
distractorRationale.d: This is a specific ecological prediction the text never supports. The passage measures water depth, says nothing about shrub survival, and gives no timeframe such as a single season.

provenance.notes: Original item built on the original soil-crust passage.

review.author: digital-sat-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Scraped plots took water to 6.1 cm versus 9.4 cm with intact crusts, so destroying the crusts means shallower penetration. C reverses the runoff logic (crusts slow runoff), B confuses infiltration with rainfall frequency, and D is an unsupported leap about shrub mortality.

review.notes: Awaiting blind independent solve before publication. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
